grammar.title: Past experience: -(으)ㄴ 적이 있어요 / 없어요
grammar.meaning: have or have never had the experience of doing something
formation: Vowel or ㄹ-ending stem + ㄴ 적이 있어요: 가다 → 간 적이 있어요
Consonant-ending stem + 은 적이 있어요: 먹다 → 먹은 적이 있어요
ㄷ irregular: 듣다 → 들은 적이 있어요
Use 없어요 for no past experience.
pitfalls: Do not place the dictionary form directly before 적.
This presents a life-history fact, while -아/어 봤어요 emphasizes trying the action.

grammar.title: Trying an action: -아/어 보다
grammar.pattern: V-아/어 보다; past polite V-아/어 봤어요
grammar.meaning: try doing something to see what it is like
formation: 먹다 → 먹어 봤어요
공부하다 → 공부해 봤어요
입다 → 입어 봤어요
듣다 → 들어 봤어요
만들다 → 만들어 봤어요
pitfalls: -아/어 봤어요 focuses on the attempt or taste, not only the historical record.
Do not replace the connective with -고.

grammar.title: When or during: -(으)ㄹ 때
grammar.meaning: when, during, or in the situation that
formation: Noun + 때 for a period or life stage: 어렸을 때
Vowel or ㄹ-ending stem + ㄹ 때: 가다 → 갈 때
Consonant-ending stem + 을 때: 먹다 → 먹을 때
Use 에 for calendar points: 월요일에, 주말에.

examples.en: I eat when I am hungry.
I have Korean class on Monday.
examples.note: A calendar point uses 에, not 때.

pitfalls: Do not use 때 after a regular weekday as if it were a continuous situation.
Do not use 에 to attach a verb clause.

grammar.title: Intention: -(으)려고 해요
grammar.meaning: intend or plan internally to do something
formation: Vowel or ㄹ-ending stem + 려고 해요: 가다 → 가려고 해요, 만들다 → 만들려고 해요
Consonant-ending stem + 으려고 해요: 먹다 → 먹으려고 해요
하다 → 하려고 해요

examples.en: I intend to go to Korea next year.
I intend to rest at home this weekend.

pitfalls: This emphasizes intention, not a fixed prediction.
Do not use the future modifier -ㄹ before 려고.

grammar.title: Soft opinion or appearance: 것 같아요
grammar.pattern: A-(으)ㄴ 것 같아요; V-는 것 같아요; past V-(으)ㄴ 것 같아요
grammar.meaning: I think, it seems, or it looks like
formation: Present descriptive verb + -(으)ㄴ: 좋다 → 좋은 것 같아요
Present action verb + -는: 오다 → 오는 것 같아요
Past action + -(으)ㄴ: 오다 → 온 것 같아요
잘하다 is an action verb: 잘하는 것 같아요.

examples.en: I think the weather is nice today.

examples.ko: 밖을 보니 비가 오는 것 같아요.
examples.en: It looks like it is raining.
examples.audioText: 밖을 보니 비가 오는 것 같아요.

pitfalls: Do not use -는 with a descriptive verb.
Keep present observation and past inference distinct.
Korean often uses this form to sound less blunt even when the speaker feels sure.

grammar.title: Native and Sino-Korean number systems
grammar.meaning: choose the number system based on the following counter or context
formation: Native numbers for age, people, objects, and hours.
Sino-Korean numbers for prices, dates, phone numbers, and minutes.
Before counters: 하나→한, 둘→두, 셋→세, 넷→네, 스물→스무.

examples.ko: 지금 오후 두 시 십오 분이에요.
examples.audioText: 지금 오후 두 시 십오 분이에요.

pitfalls: Hours are Native Korean, but minutes are Sino-Korean.
Do not say 하나 시, 둘 명, or 스물 살.

grammar.title: Calendar dates and irregular month names
grammar.pattern: Sino number + 월 + Sino number + 일
grammar.meaning: state months and days of the month
formation: June is 유월, not 육월.
October is 시월, not 십월.
Ask 오늘은 몇 월 며칠이에요?
pitfalls: Use 유월 and 시월 for natural pronunciation.

grammar.title: Plain, aspirated, and tense consonants
grammar.meaning: distinguish consonants by aspiration and muscle tension
formation: Plain consonants are relaxed.
Aspirated consonants release a strong burst of air.
Tense consonants use tight, controlled pressure with very little air.
Accuracy and physical tension matter more than speed or loudness.
pitfalls: Do not add a large puff of air to a tense consonant.

prompt.stem: Choose the correctly formed past-experience sentence.

choices.why: -는 describes a present action, not a completed experience.
Correct: 가다 becomes 간 before 적.
A vowel-ending stem takes -ㄴ, not -은.
-ㄹ points forward and does not form this past-experience pattern.

prompt.stem: Choose the correctly formed present observation.

choices.why: This normally points to a past event: it seems it rained.
Correct: A present action verb takes -는 것 같아요.

This combines unrelated time and similarity forms.

exercises.explanation: Present action: 오는 것 같아요. Past inference: 온 것 같아요.

prompt.stem: Which line uses the correct number systems for 2:15?

Correct: Hours use Native 두 and minutes use Sino 십오.
둘 contracts to 두 before 시.
Minutes use Sino 십오, not Native 열다섯.

exercises.explanation: Hours are Native Korean; minutes are Sino-Korean.

prompt.stem: Ask for three apples naturally.

choices.why: 개 normally takes Native Korean numbers.
Correct: 셋 contracts to 세 before 개.
셋 must contract before a counter.
명 counts people, not objects.

exercises.explanation: Use 세 개 for three items.

prompt.stem: Fix the age expression.

exercises.explanation: 스물 contracts to 스무 before the counter 살.

prompt.stem: Complete the contrast: There is rice, but no kimchi.

choices.why: 를 would mark an action target, but nothing is acting on kimchi.
Correct: 은/는 sets up the explicit contrast between rice and kimchi.
Object particles do not mark simple existence.
이/가 is possible for neutral existence, but it does not express the intended contrast as clearly.

exercises.explanation: Contrast uses 밥은 있어요, 김치는 없어요.

prompt.stem: 밥___ 있어요. 밥___ 먹어요.
prompt.stemEn: There is rice. I eat rice.

exercises.explanation: 이 marks neutral existence; 을 marks the thing receiving the action.

prompt.stem: Fix the action-place particle.

exercises.explanation: 공부하다 is an action, so the action place takes 에서.

prompt.stem: 저는 주말___ 오후 두 시___ 카페___ 친구___ 만나요.
prompt.audioText: 저는 주말에 오후 두 시에 카페에서 친구를 만나요.
prompt.stemEn: On the weekend at 2 PM, I meet a friend at a cafe.

strict: 저는 주말에 오후 두 시에 카페에서 친구를 만나요
relaxed: 저는 주말에 오후 두 시에 카페에서 친구를 만나요

exercises.explanation: Time points take 에, an action place takes 에서, and the person met takes 를.

prompt.stem: Choose the pair that clearly marks a recipient and then a source.

choices.why: These reverse source and recipient.
Correct: 에게 marks the recipient; 에게서 clearly marks the person something came from.
에서 is not used for a person in this contrast.
께서 is an honorific subject marker, not a source marker.

exercises.explanation: 친구에게 선물을 줘요, 친구에게서 편지를 받아요.

prompt.stem: Fix the honorific recipient marker.

exercises.explanation: 께 is the respectful recipient marker and matches 드렸어요.

prompt.stem: Which form follows the ㄹ-final noun 길?

choices.why: ㄹ-final nouns are the exception and do not take 으로.
Correct: After a ㄹ-final noun, use 로.
Do not stack 에 and 로 here.
에서 marks an action place or source, not direction along a route.

exercises.explanation: 받침 ㄹ is the exception: 길로.

prompt.stem: A manager blames you for food you did not throw away. Which reaction fits?

choices.why: This means you grew attached.
Correct: 억울하다 expresses being wrongly blamed or treated unfairly.
This means someone reads social cues quickly.
This denies frustration and misses the injustice.

exercises.explanation: Use 억울하다 for the burning feeling of being unfairly blamed.

prompt.stem: The office is tense and quiet, but someone enters singing loudly. Which description fits?

choices.why: This describes warmth or affection.
Correct: The person is missing the mood and social cues.
No one is being wrongly blamed in this situation.
This would mean carefully watching reactions, which the person is not doing.

exercises.explanation: 눈치가 없다 means failing to read the room.

strict: 이 오래된 가방은 정이 들어서 버릴 수가 없어요
relaxed: 이 오래된 가방은 정이 들어서 버릴 수가 없어요

exercises.explanation: 정이 들다 means to grow attached over time.

prompt.stem: Which word begins with the tense ㅉ sound and means salty?

choices.why: 자요 begins with plain ㅈ and means sleeps.
Correct: 짜요 begins with tense ㅉ and means salty.
차요 begins with aspirated ㅊ and has a different meaning.
싸요 begins with tense ㅆ and means cheap.

exercises.explanation: ㅉ is a tight tense consonant with little extra air.

prompt.stem: Which syllable starts with tense ㅃ?

choices.why: 분 begins with plain ㅂ.
Correct: 뿔 begins with tense ㅃ.
풀 begins with aspirated ㅍ.
불 begins with plain ㅂ.

exercises.explanation: Tense ㅃ uses firm lip pressure and very little air.

prompt.stem: Listen for the tense consonant and type the sentence.

exercises.explanation: 짜요 starts with tense ㅉ.

prompt.stem: Put the chunks in order, then read the result slowly.

exercises.explanation: Read accurately and keep the tense ㄸ controlled rather than loud.

prompt.stem: Put the consequence sentence in order.
prompt.stemEn: The road is slippery, so I have no choice but to wear skates.

relaxed: 길이 미끄러워서 스케이트를 신을 수밖에 없어요

exercises.modelAnswer: 길이 미끄러워서 스케이트를 신을 수밖에 없어요
exercises.explanation: -아서 gives the reason; -(으)ㄹ 수밖에 없어요 says there is no other choice.

prompt.stem: Which connector is the more formal equivalent of therefore?

choices.why: 하지만 means but.
Correct: 그러므로 means therefore in a formal style.
게다가 means in addition.
그리고 means and or and then.

exercises.explanation: 그러므로 is a formal therefore connector.

prompt.stem: Fix the past polite form of 만들다.

exercises.explanation: 만들다 becomes 만들었어요 in the polite past.
